source_claims.statement: Recon on /s/sfsites/aura endpoints. Initial reflections HTML-encoded due to text/plain. Script tags filtered.
Focused on Aura/Lightning. aura.tag reflected; aura.format=JSON changed content type to text/html. SVG onload bypassed script filtering.

research_questions.formulation: Can an Aura parameter that reflects be made to render as HTML and execute despite encoding and script filtering?
research_questions.anchor: introduction of aura.format=JSON after initial reflection failed verification
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether content type can be controlled and script filters bypassed
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that text/plain or script filtering closes the XSS

systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: Salesforce-specific parameter combinations (aura.format) and SVG after standard XSS failed

negative_inconclusive: Initial reflections encoded due to text/plain
unobserved_history: exact training data influence on Aura knowledge
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat early encoding as proof of no XSS
The working combination required both content-type control and non-script payload
next_evidence_actions: Note CVD reporting and Salesforce remediation
layer_b_candidate_principles: When a parameter reflects but content type prevents execution, test framework-specific parameters that may change response content type
SVG event handlers can serve as an alternative when script tags are filtered
model_vs_harness: Knowing Aura-specific parameters is model/domain knowledge; systematic parameter testing and content-type observation can be harness.
